You're likely looking for someone local who can explain how lenders will assess your day rate and contract history. iComply can introduce you to a suitable mortgage broker in the UK who specialises in contractor mortgages, and they will quote you directly.

context_heading: Understanding contractor mortgages and finding the right broker
context: Contractor mortgages let lenders assess your income based on your day rate and contract rather than your company accounts. Some lenders specialise in this, but not all brokers deal with them. A good broker will explain which lenders are likely to accept your situation and why.

Mortgage advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Any broker or adviser you use should be authorised, or be an appointed representative of an authorised firm, and you can check this on the FCA register. Brokers must also tell you whether they search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders, and how they are paid.

questions_heading: Questions to ask the mortgage broker
questions: Are you authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, or an appointed representative of an authorised firm?
Do you search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders?

faqs.q: What is a contractor mortgage and why might I need one?
faqs.a: A contractor mortgage is a mortgage where the lender assesses your income based on your day rate and contract rather than your limited company accounts. If you're a contractor, this can make it easier to borrow because your income isn't shown in the same way as a salaried employee's.

faqs.q: How can I check if a mortgage broker is authorised?
faqs.a: You can check whether a broker or adviser is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) on the FCA register. They should be authorised or an appointed representative of an authorised firm, and they must tell you how they are paid.

faqs.q: Does IR35 affect my mortgage application?
faqs.a: IR35 status can affect how lenders assess your income. Some lenders may treat income from inside IR35 contracts differently, so it's worth discussing your situation with a broker who understands contractor mortgages.

faqs.q: What if I have a short contract history or gaps between contracts?
faqs.a: Some lenders are more flexible than others when it comes to contract history and gaps. A broker who deals with contractors can explain which lenders are likely to consider your situation.

extra_heading: Weighing up 'top' and 'near me' for contractor mortgages
extra: When you search for a top contractor mortgage near me, the word top is doing a lot of work. There is no official ranking of mortgage brokers, so no one can honestly call themselves the best. What you can do is judge each broker on what matters to you: whether they regularly arrange mortgages for day-rate contractors, whether they explain how lenders will read your contract history, and whether their answers about IR35 and lender criteria make sense to you.

Near me is worth thinking about too. Many brokers now work by phone, email and video, so a firm in another part of the UK may suit you better than one on your high street if they clearly understand contractor income. If meeting face to face matters to you, say so when you enquire, and we will take that into account when introducing you to a broker.

Comparing brokers is easier once you know what to ask. Ask each one whether they search the whole of the market or a limited panel, how they are paid, and whether they charge a fee as well as receiving commission from the lender. Ask them to talk you through how they would present your day rate and contract length to a lender, and listen for specifics rather than general reassurance.

extra_faqs.q: Can I rely on a broker calling themselves the top contractor mortgage specialist?
extra_faqs.a: There is no official body that ranks mortgage brokers as top or best, so treat such wording as a marketing claim rather than a fact. Instead, check that the broker is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority or is an appointed representative of an authorised firm, and ask how they assess contractor income.

extra_faqs.q: Do I have to choose a broker who is physically near me?
extra_faqs.a: No. What matters most is that the broker understands contractor mortgages and can explain how lenders will view your day rate, contract history and IR35 position. If you would rather deal with someone local, tell us when you enquire and we will factor that in.
